en: 10. The Pairs on the Faculties (Indriyayamaka) 10.3.
The Section on Full Understanding (Pariññāvāra) 10.3.5.
The Section on the Present and the Future (Paccuppannānāgatavāra)
10.3.5.1. Positive Order (Anuloma) He who fully understands the eye-faculty will abandon the faculty of mental grief? No.
Or again, he who will abandon the faculty of mental grief fully understands the eye-faculty? No.
Is it the case that whoever fully understands the eye-faculty will cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"? No.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever will cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" has already fully understood the eye-faculty? No.
Is it the case that whoever fully understands the eye-faculty will cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*)? No.
Or, is it that whoever will develop the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya) also fully understands the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya)? No.
Is it that whoever fully understands the faculty of the eye will realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya)? Yes.
Or, is it that whoever will realize the faculty of one who has already known also fully understands the faculty of the eye?
Seven persons will realize the faculty of one who has already known, but they do not fully understand the faculty of the eye.
One who possesses the highest path will both realize the faculty of one who has already known and fully understand the faculty of the eye. (Based on the faculty of the eye.
Is it the case that whoever abandons the faculty of mental grief will cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"? No.
Or, whoever will cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya), will that person abandon the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya)? No.
Whoever abandons the faculty of mental grief, will that person cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)? Yes.
Or, whoever will cultivate the faculty of final knowledge, will that person abandon the faculty of mental grief?

Six persons will cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*), but they do not abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*). One who possesses the path of the non-returner (*anāgāmimagga*) will both cultivate the faculty of final knowledge and abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Is it the case that whoever abandons the faculty of mental grief will realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever will realize the faculty of one who has already known will abandon the faculty of mental grief?
Seven persons will realize the faculty of one who has already known, but they do not abandon the faculty of mental grief.
One who possesses the path of non-returning will both realize the faculty of one who has already known and abandon the faculty of mental grief.
(Based on the faculty of mental grief.)
Is it the case that whoever develops the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" will develop the faculty of final knowledge? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever will develop the faculty of final knowledge develops the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"?

Six types of persons will develop the faculty of final knowledge, but they do not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown. The eighth person (the Sotāpatti-magga-samangi) will develop both the faculty of final knowledge and the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
Is it the case that whoever develops the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown” will realize the faculty of one who has already known? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever will realize the faculty of one who has already known develops the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown”?
Seven types of persons will realize the faculty of one who has already known, yet they do not develop the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown.”
The person at the eighth stage will realize the faculty of one who has already known and develops the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
(Based on the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
He who develops the faculty of final knowledge will realize the faculty of one who has already known? Yes.
Or again, does he who will realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya) cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)?

Five types of persons will realize the faculty of one who has already known, but they do not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge. Three possessors of the path will both realize the faculty of one who has already known and cultivate the faculty of final knowledge. (Based on the faculty of final knowledge. 10.3.5.2.
Negative (Paccanīka)
He who does not fully understand the faculty of the eye will not abandon the faculty of mental grief?

Five types of persons do not fully understand the faculty of the eye, yet they will not fail to abandon the faculty of mental grief. Four types of persons neither fully understand the faculty of the eye nor will they abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Or conversely, he who will not abandon the faculty of mental grief does not fully understand the faculty of the eye?

One who possesses the highest path (agga-maggasamaṅgī) will not abandon the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya), but he does not fail to fully understand the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya). Four types of persons neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor do they fully understand the faculty of the eye.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the faculty of the eye will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)?

Those worldlings (puthujjana) who will attain the path do not fully understand the faculty of the eye, but they are not [persons] who do not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
They will not cultivate it. Eight persons do not fully understand the eye-faculty (*cakkhundriya*) and will not cultivate the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*).
Or rather, is it the case that whoever does not cultivate the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty does not fully understand the eye-faculty?
One who possesses the supreme path (*aggamagga-samaṅgī*) does not cultivate the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty, but [it is] not that he does not [fully understand] the eye-faculty.
He fully understands. Eight persons will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*) and will not fully understand the eye-faculty (*cakkhundriya*).
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the eye-faculty will not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*)?

Seven persons do not fully understand the eye-faculty, yet they will not fail to cultivate the faculty of final knowledge. Two persons neither fully understand the eye-faculty nor will they cultivate the faculty of final knowledge.
Or again, is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya) does not fully understand the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya)?

One who possesses the path of the supreme fruit (agga-magga-samaṅgī) does not develop the faculty of final knowledge, but he does not fail to fully understand the faculty of the eye. Two types of persons neither develop the faculty of final knowledge nor do they fully understand the faculty of the eye.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the faculty of the eye will not realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya)?

Seven persons do not fully understand the eye-faculty (*cakkhundriya*), yet they will realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*). Two persons neither fully understand the eye-faculty nor will they realize the faculty of one who has already known.
Is it the case that whoever will not realize the faculty of one who has already known does not fully understand the eye-faculty? Yes. (Based on the eye-faculty.
Is it the case that whoever does not abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*) will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*)?
Those worldlings who will attain the path do not abandon the faculty of mental grief, yet it is not the case that they will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Eight types of persons neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor will they cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever does not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" does not abandon the faculty of mental grief?

One who possesses the path of the non-returner (anāgāmimagga) will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya), yet it is not the case that he does not abandon the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya).
Eight types of persons neither cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor do they abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Is it the case that whoever does not abandon the faculty of mental grief will not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)?

Six persons do not abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*), yet it is not the case that they will not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*). Three persons neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor will they cultivate the faculty of final knowledge.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever will not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge does not abandon the faculty of mental grief? Yes.
Is it the case that whoever does not abandon the faculty of mental grief will not realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)?

Seven types of persons do not abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*), yet it is not the case that they will not realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*). Two types of persons neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor will they realize the faculty of one who has already known.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever will not realize the faculty of one who has already known does not abandon the faculty of mental grief? Yes, it is so. (Based on the faculty of mental grief.
Is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*) will not develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*)?

Six persons do not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet they will not fail to develop the faculty of final knowledge. Three persons neither develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor will they develop the faculty of final knowledge.
Is it the case that whoever will not develop the faculty of final knowledge also does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"? Yes.
Is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" will not realize the faculty of one who has already known?
Seven persons do not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet they will not fail to realize the faculty of one who has known.
Two persons neither develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor will they realize the faculty of one who has known.

Is it the case that whoever will not realize the faculty of one who has known does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"? Yes. (Based on the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.")
Is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*) will not realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)?

Five types of persons do not develop the faculty of final knowledge, yet they will not fail to realize the faculty of one who has already known. Two types of persons neither develop the faculty of final knowledge nor will they realize the faculty of one who has already known.
Or conversely, is it the case that whoever will not realize the faculty of one who has already known does not develop the faculty of final knowledge? Yes. (Based on the faculty of final knowledge.)
